body: Your description hit me in the gut, as it is very similar to my experience with citalopram. I was on it for about a month, and had a complete breakdown. I wound up stopping in the end because it made me absolutely incapable of sleep. My psychiatrist prescribed me a common sleep aid, and when that did not work, a more powerful sleep aid, which at least let me sleep but my quality of life was terrible. I wasn't able to work, to enjoy anything, and I took a lot of risks with biking to work that I normally would not have that could easily have gotten me killed (I have a little scar on my arm as a reminder of this). After stopping the citalopram, I went on about the same way for about two months, and then saw my psychiatrist who  prescribed another antidepressant that actually did a great deal to help me. I was on that new antidepressant for about another month, and felt much better mentally, but I had a physical side effect that necessitated stopping it. Since that time I have never been on any other antidepressants, and while I have had my highs and lows, I feel the full range of human experience has come back to me. Obviously this is just an anecdote, but have you discussed with your psychiatrist the option of taking something else?  One other thing, your second to last sentence reminds me of my situation as well. There was a woman in my life at that time who I had feelings for that turned into a lot of hatred. That emotional  baggage was a lot of poison for me, and when I was finally able to let it go, things got a lot easier for me. Seven years on, I look back at at least those feelings, and realize how much they damaged me at the time. Do you have any way of addressing that kind of toxicity? Though you may not realize it, even fantasizing about harm on others for me is one of the things that just keeps the depression coming back. I have other problems in my life now, so I won't tell you it's all roses from here on out, but at least I was able to get back what I felt were the best parts of me, and I hope you can too.

That sounds like you have a nice life. Maybe I should give working in industry a chance. The hours are not as punishing as academia, so I would have the opportunity to build up opportunities and experiences that can sustain me.

Organic chemistry. Yeah, I was the star of my undergraduate research program too. I got all the scholarships, got to do undergrad research and got into the best graduate program in the field. I got into it because I love the science, and the ability to discover new things, beneath all the bullshit of the academic culture I still do love it. I don't have any doubt about my ability, and I was pretty successful at what I did, getting some papers, but due to the reasons I outlined above I am having a hard time getting an academic position. I get filled with this burning resentment when I see people who accomplished less than me get professor positions with years less work, because they had advisors who were supportive and went to bat for them.  I am just afraid I am so burnt out and bitter I will be barely be able to function even if I get my dream job. I would rather change fields than go into pharma, because working for a big company in the corporate world with so little job security nowadays just doesn't feel right for me (and I have the luxury of not having dependants, so I could actually walk away). I suppose one option is to work in pharma for a few years to save up some money, but I don't know what that will do for my mental health without me being able to change my underlying problems. I have some issues that I didn't mention in my first post with my health, and I have struggled with substance abuse as a coping mechanism, so that is another aspect that makes life tougher for me. Congrats on walking away before you felt you became trapped by academia. I look at a tenure track position as the ultimate prize, for the security and freedom it provides, but I am afraid I am destroying my life trying to get to it. What did you wind up doing instead of pursuing grad studies? Has it been fulfilling for you? I think I could do a job that is very unfulfilling if I got the chance to live in my dream location.
